issues.legal_issue: A possession decree cannot be entered on the pleadings when the defendant has clearly disputed a material element of the plaintiff’s termination case and the pleadings contain no clear and unequivocal admission entitling the plaintiff to possession.
material_facts: The plaintiffs sought possession on the basis that the tenancy had expired and had been terminated by notice.
The defendant disputed that the tenancy had expired or been determined, while not denying receipt of the notice.
The plaintiffs sought judgment on admission, relying on the asserted landlord-tenant relationship and service of the notice; the defendant denied admitting termination.
The plaintiffs relied only on the pleadings as the source of any admission.
The lower courts entered a possession decree on admission.
issues.conclusion: The pleadings contained no clear admission of the plaintiffs’ case on termination of the tenancy, so the possession decree could not stand. The judgments below were set aside and the suit was remanded for trial without any observation on its merits.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XII Rule 6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, judgment on admission requires a clear, unambiguous and unequivocal admission that plainly entitles the opposing party to the requested order; it is not enough that a fact such as service of notice is not denied when the material claim of termination is disputed. Uttam Singh Duggal & Co. Ltd. v. United Bank of India states that the rule applies where admitted facts make it impossible for the admitting party to succeed. Karam Kapahi v. Lal Chand Public Charitable Trust involved a clear admission of non-payment and does not justify judgment where the material admission is absent. The court also relied on Gilbert v. Smith, Hughes v. London, Edinburgh, and Glasgow Assurance Company, Landergan v. Feast, Koramall Ramballav v. Mongilal Dalimchand, J.C. Galstaun v. E.D. Sassoon & Co., and Abdul Rahman and Brothers v. Parbati Devi for the requirement of a clear admission.

rule.if: possession_suit and plaintiff_sought_judgment_on_pleadings and defendant_disputed_termination and no_clear_admission_entitling_possession

predicates.possession_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking possession of premises from a defendant in possession.
predicates.plaintiff_sought_judgment_on_pleadings: The plaintiff asked the court to grant judgment on the basis of admissions in the pleadings.
predicates.defendant_disputed_termination: The defendant denied that the tenancy had expired or been determined, even though receipt of the notice was not denied.
predicates.no_clear_admission_entitling_possession: The pleadings contained no clear and unequivocal admission of facts that entitled the plaintiff to possession.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff seeks judgment on the pleadings in a possession suit, a defendant’s dispute of termination and the absence of a clear admission entitling the plaintiff to possession mean that a possession decree on admission is unwarranted.
